text: Filters narrow a list down to the records that actually matter, and breadcrumbs show you exactly what's filtering it, in plain English, without ever reopening a menu.

Above every list is a filter icon that opens the condition builder: a row with a field, an operator, and a value — Priority, is, 1 - Critical. Click Run and the list narrows to only matching records. Add a second condition row and an AND/OR toggle lets you combine them — AND narrows further, OR widens. Stack several conditions and you've built a real, specific query without writing a line of code.

Once a filter runs, the area above the column headers replaces the plain table label with breadcrumbs — small pills reading something like Priority is 1 - Critical, chained together with the AND or OR you chose. Breadcrumbs exist so nobody has to reopen the condition builder just to remember what's filtering the list. Click any single breadcrumb and it reopens the builder scoped to just that one condition.

A filter you expect to reuse doesn't have to be rebuilt every time. You can save the current filter as a Personal list view, visible only to you, or share it so a whole team sees the same pre-filtered view by default. That's exactly how a view like Service Desk view, from the last lesson, comes to exist in the first place.

Every filter you build through breadcrumbs is, underneath, translated into a compact text string called an encoded query — the same syntax ServiceNow uses as the sysparm_query URL parameter. Active incidents, Priority 1 might encode as active=true caret priority=1, where the caret means AND. You don't need to write these by hand day to day, but that string is exactly what a bookmarked list's URL contains.

Condition builder for building, breadcrumbs for reading and editing, saved views for reuse, encoded queries underneath it all. Next up: related lists — how a form surfaces records from other tables that point back at it.
